Shows and commands in Gladys the **Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi** switches,
dimmers and plugs (United States, Canada) of your **My Leviton** account,
through the Leviton cloud.

> **Unofficial API, never tested with a real account.** The integration talks
> to the API of the My Leviton app, which Leviton does not document and may
> change at any time. It was written from the decora-wifi library (the one of
> the Home Assistant integration) and schmittx's Home Assistant integration,
> and tested with made-up answers only. Not affiliated with Leviton.

## What you get

One Gladys device per supported Leviton device:

| Leviton device                       | Gladys features                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Dimmer (DW6HD, D26HD, DW1KD, D2ELV…) | On/Off (light, `light/binary`), Brightness (0 to 100), Online |
| Switch (DW15S, D215S…)               | On/Off (switch, `switch/binary`), Online                      |
| Plug (DW15P, DW15A, D215P, D215O…)   | On/Off (switch, `switch/binary`), Online                      |

- **Brightness**: 0 turns the light off; any other value turns it on, within
  the minimum and maximum levels set in the app.
- **Online** (1 = yes, read only): what Leviton says of the device. An
  offline device is also marked "unreachable" on its card; its last known
  state stays shown, not updated while it is offline, and its commands are
  refused.
- **Unknown model**: a device whose model is not in the lists of the
  integration is shown read only (no command) until the integration knows
  it.
- **Consumption**: Leviton gives none for these devices in the known
  libraries: there is none here.
- **Fans** (DW4SF, D24SF), **button controllers** (DW4BC), the **bridge**
  (MLWSB) and the **GFCI outlets** (D2GF1, D2GF2: a ground-fault protection is
  not a plug to cut from Gladys) are not shown in this version.

Lights (`light/binary`), switches and plugs (`switch/binary`) are ordinary
Gladys commands: an "everything off" of Gladys, of a voice assistant or of a
scene turns them off too. Do not plug in a device that must never be cut.

## Setup

1. In Gladys, install the **Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi** integration from the
   store.
2. Enter the **e-mail** and **password** of your My Leviton account (the ones
   of the app), then save: saving starts the sign-in.
3. If the status says "Sign-in required", click **Test the connection**; if
   it says a verification code is asked, see below.
4. Open the **Discovery** tab and add the devices.

The password field is a `secret` field: Gladys keeps it in its database (in
clear, as any configuration value, and in its backups), never shows it again,
and the integration sends it only to My Leviton (`my.leviton.com`). It is used
for the sign-ins only: the session obtained is kept and reused at every read
and after a restart, until it ends.

### When does the integration sign in?

A sign-in without code makes Leviton e-mail a code to an account that uses
two-factor authentication. So the integration signs in by itself (start,
reconnection to Gladys, session renewal, spaced new try) **only for an
account whose sign-in without code was accepted before** (it notes it in its
`/data`). For any other account, or when its `/data` is lost, it waits for a
click: the status says "Sign-in required: click Test the connection", with
no automatic new try. A click is: saving the configuration, and the buttons
of the configuration screen.

An account known "without code" that turns two-factor authentication on
later may get **at most one e-mail**, at the next automatic sign-in; it is
then noted as a code account and never signed in again without a click.

### Verification code (two-factor authentication)

If your My Leviton account uses two-factor authentication, Leviton e-mails a
code at each sign-in without code. The integration then stops and the status
says so:

1. Under **Verify the code**, type the code of the last Leviton e-mail and
   click the button. "Code accepted" means connected.
2. No e-mail, or the code is too old? Click **Send the verification code**:
   the integration signs in without code and Leviton e-mails a new one (at
   most once a minute).

The integration never sends a code without your click, never keeps it, and
never signs in again by itself for an account that asks for a code: the
session is kept as long as Leviton accepts it; when it refuses it, the
integration stops and asks you for a code again.

## Refresh

The devices are read every **60 seconds** by default (30 to 60, _Refresh
interval_), **one request per residence**; the list of residences is read
again every hour. A residence in error keeps its last devices (marked
"unreachable") without stopping the reads of the others.

A command leaves at once; the value Leviton confirms is shown at once, the
device is read again 2 seconds later, and a slightly late read does not undo
the commanded value (15 seconds). The commands of one device go one after
the other. Gladys waits 5 seconds for the answer: a command that has not left
3 seconds after the click (queue, sign-in in progress, slow network) is
refused **without having been sent**; a command sent but slow is answered at
4.3 seconds and its effect shows afterwards.

## Troubleshooting

- **E-mail or password refused**: the integration stops, even after a
  restart, and tries again once after 6 hours then every 24 hours (only for
  an account known "without code"; otherwise it waits for a click). Fix them
  and save, or click _Test the connection_.
- **Too many failed sign-ins** (refused by Leviton): a one-hour pause,
  commands and buttons included, kept after a restart.
- **Session refused**: one single new sign-in; refused again, the
  integration pauses and tries again after 1 hour, 6 hours, then every 24
  hours. _Test the connection_ tries again at once.
- **Too many requests (429)**: a pause of 1 minute to 6 hours (Leviton's
  `Retry-After`, 15 minutes without it), for the reads, the commands and the
  buttons, kept after a restart or a reconnection to Gladys.
- **HTTP 403** of the reads: a 403 of one residence pauses nothing (it keeps
  its last devices). When every residence answers 403, the integration first
  signs in again once (as for a refused token), only for an account known
  "without code"; if the 403 stays, or for any other account, a one-hour
  pause.
- **Leviton unavailable (5xx, network)**: new tries after 1, 2, 5, 10, then
  every 15 minutes, never sooner than the interval.

## Limits

- Unofficial API: Leviton may change it, block it or ask for more checks.
- No live updates (the websocket of the app): one read every 30 to 60
  seconds.
- One My Leviton account per Gladys, ten residences at most.
- No fans, GFCI outlets, motion sensor (D2MSD: the light only), scenes,
  schedules nor settings (LEDs, fade…) in this version.
- Never tested with a real account: please report what you see on the
  [GitHub repository](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-leviton/issues)
  (without your e-mail, password or codes).

## Privacy

The integration keeps in `/data/leviton-state.json` (readable by its own
container only): the session token, the Leviton user id and the end of the
token, the account they belong to as a hash of the e-mail, the accounts
(hashes) known "without code" and those that ask for a code, the time of the
last code request, the end of a pause, and a stop on refused credentials tied
to a salted fingerprint of the e-mail and password. Neither the e-mail, the
password nor the codes. The MAC address, serial number and local IP address
of the devices are not sent to Gladys. Nothing is sent anywhere but to My
Leviton.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your My Leviton account | `section` | No | Shows the Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi devices of your My Leviton account in Gladys: switches and plugs (on/off), dimmers (on/off, brightness), and whether each device is online. Enter the e-mail and password of the My Leviton app, save, then add the devices from the Discovery tab. If your account asks for a verification code, use the two buttons below. Read every 60 seconds. Fans and button controllers are not shown in this version. Unofficial API, never tested with a real account. Not affiliated with Leviton. |
| My Leviton e-mail | `string` | Sí |  |
| My Leviton password | `secret` | Sí | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to My Leviton (my.leviton.com). |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | Seconds between two reads of the devices (30 to 60): one request per residence each time. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the feature names of the devices added from now on, and for the command errors. |

## Cómo instalar Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-leviton:0.1.1`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-leviton](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-leviton).

Leviton Decora Smart Wi-Fi requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.
